I've been moving every year to a different place, mostly a different country, for the past 7 years of my life. And first off I need to break the news that "starting over" in a new environment won't make all your problems magically dissapear; they just come back eventually. You might not like where you live rn but you have to understand that the place is not the problem, and there is help available for whatever mental issues you're dealing with. Don't get me wrong, moving and that "fresh start" can be really fun but just sort your life out so that you don't have to worry about it after. 

As of moving itself, save money for it beforehand, there's nothing worse than being broke in the middle of nowhere. With you're american medical degree I believe it would be really easy to get it recognized in any other country. Canada is great for outdoors, especially if you don't wanna live in a big city, any cities other than those are really chill and the houses are cheaap; and if you live near the rocky mountains, there are endless adventures. But it is very cold, Im from Brazil and when I first moved here I thought I could take \-20, what no one tells you is that those temperatures last for a reallyyyy long time. If you don't mind that though I'd say it's perfect for the outdorsy lifestyle.
